skill.name: okx-agent-payments-protocol
skill.description: Guides OKX OnchainOS workflows for x402, MPP channels, subscriptions, and agent-to-agent payments across supported EVM networks.
skill.summary: Handle x402, MPP, subscription, and agent-to-agent payments with OKX OnchainOS.
skill.author: okx

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown syntax, fixed documentation links, or protocol literals rather than executable threats. Confirmed risks include local private-key access and unattended installer execution. Critical semantic review found an A2A payment path that signs seller-controlled terms without buyer confirmation.

remediation.issue: The A2A buyer path signs seller-controlled payment terms without preview or confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Fetch and display amount, token, network, recipient, and expiry, then require explicit confirmation before any signature.

remediation.issue: The quote workflow probes arbitrary supplied URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and block loopback, private, link-local, metadata, redirect, and DNS-rebinding destinations before every request.

remediation.issue: Preflight installs or updates executable code and obeys dynamic action text.
remediation.suggestion: Pin verified artifacts, require user approval for installs and updates, and treat data.action as display-only data.

remediation.issue: Session vouchers may increase after seller-controlled price changes.
remediation.suggestion: Display every changed unit price and cumulative authorization, then require explicit confirmation before signing a higher voucher.

remediation.issue: The local-key fallback reads EVM_PRIVATE_KEY from host configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Remove local-key signing or require a dedicated secure signer that never exposes key material to the agent process.

remediation.issue: User-controlled values are shown in shell command templates without mandatory escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured argument arrays and reject shell interpretation for URLs, descriptions, realms, identifiers, addresses, and parameters.

semantic_findings.description: Preflight updates the binary and skill checkout, obeys dynamic action text, and runs a remote README installer without explicit approval.

content.user_title: Handle Agent Payments Across x402 and MPP
content.value_statement: Agent payment protocols require careful routing, decoding, signing, and settlement tracking. This skill guides supported OKX OnchainOS payment workflows through one dispatcher.
actual_capabilities: Routes x402, MPP charge, MPP session, subscription, A2MCP, and A2A payment requests.
Quotes supported endpoints and presents network, token, amount, recipient, and scheme details.
Creates payment links, pays payment identifiers, and checks settlement status.
Opens, tops up, uses, and closes MPP payment channels.
Subscribes, changes, cancels, and inspects supported recurring payments.
Decodes payment receipts and reports transaction or settlement status.
limitations: Requires the OnchainOS CLI, a compatible wallet session, network access, and supported payment endpoints.
Most signing paths support EVM networks only, and local-key support covers fewer schemes.
The A2A buyer flow lacks its own payment preview and confirmation gate.
Endpoint safety, seller identity, token contracts, and payment terms require independent verification.

use_cases.title: Integrate Paid APIs
use_cases.description: Quote an HTTP 402 endpoint, inspect available payment methods, confirm terms, and replay the paid request.

use_cases.title: Operate Payment Channels
use_cases.description: Open an MPP channel, track vouchers and prepaid balance, add funds, and close the channel.

use_cases.title: Manage Recurring Access
use_cases.description: Subscribe to a protected resource, prove access, change plans, inspect allowances, or cancel service.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Payment Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this HTTP 402 response from [URL]. Explain the payment terms and stop before signing or paying.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one protected endpoint

prompt_templates.title: Create a Payment Link
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A2A payment link for [amount] [token] to [recipient]. Show every submitted term and return the payment identifier.
prompt_templates.scenario: Seller requests payment from another agent

prompt_templates.title: Compare Payment Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote [endpoint] with [method] and [parameters]. Compare supported schemes, show the recommended option, and wait for my confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Manage an MPP Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Manage the MPP session for [endpoint] using channel [channel_id]. Track deposits, vouchers, spending, top-ups, closing, and refunds with explicit confirmations.

output_examples.input: Quote a paid weather endpoint before paying.
output_examples.output: Payment approval requested: Base network, 0.01 USDC, specified recipient, and one request. Waiting for explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Create a payment link for 25 USDT.
output_examples.output: Payment link created for 25 USDT to the supplied recipient. The payment identifier and shareable delivery link are ready.
Channel closed. The final charge, refunded balance, and settlement transaction are reported.

best_practices: Verify the endpoint, network, token, amount, recipient, and expiry before every signature.
Prefer TEE-backed signing and keep private keys outside agent-readable files and environment variables.
Use public HTTPS endpoint allowlists and apply strict limits to subscriptions, allowances, and channel deposits.
anti_patterns: Do not pay an A2A identifier until its server terms match a trusted out-of-band agreement.
Do not bypass confirmation because a similar payment or seller was approved earlier.
Do not grant unlimited Permit2 allowance or expose a local private key for convenience.

faq.question: Which payment protocols are supported?
faq.answer: The skill covers x402 accepts schemes, MPP charge and session flows, period subscriptions, A2MCP, and A2A payment identifiers.

faq.question: Can this skill move funds?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create signatures and authorizations that sellers or facilitators settle on-chain.

faq.question: Does every payment require confirmation?
faq.answer: Most x402 flows require confirmation. The bundled A2A buyer flow does not, so add a preview gate before use.

faq.question: Can it use a local private key?
faq.answer: Some accepts-based schemes support local signing through EVM_PRIVATE_KEY. TEE-backed wallet signing is safer and supports more workflows.

faq.question: Which networks are supported?
faq.answer: The documented signing flows focus on EVM networks. Unsupported chains stop with an error.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The OnchainOS CLI and a compatible wallet session are required. Paid operations also need network connectivity and sufficient token balance.
